features.name: Session events
features.does: The room's raw event log: joins, published tracks, disconnects with reasons.
features.value: Exact answers to 'who dropped and why'.
features.ask: When a call goes wrong today, can you tell whether it was the network or the agent?

features.name: Session analytics
features.does: The default view of a call: room facts, session timeline, publishers/subscribers, egresses, bandwidth and connection quality/latency.
features.value: Rules the network in or out before anyone blames the AI.
features.ask: When a call goes wrong today, can you tell whether it was the network or the agent?

features.name: Sessions List
features.does: Searchable history of every room/call with time range, filters and a Features column that flags sessions with agent insights.
features.value: Find the exact call a customer complained about in seconds.
features.say: Every conversation your agent has lands here, searchable, and the ones with full agent recordings are flagged so you can jump straight in.
features.ask: When a customer complains about a bad call, how does your team find that specific call today?
features.limits: Default range is Past 24 hours; widen it to find older calls.
features.ask_technical: Do you key sessions to your own call or customer IDs (room names, metadata) so support can search them?

features.name: Session Analytics
features.does: Shows who joined, from where and which region, connection and timeline for the room.
features.value: Rules out a caller's bad connection before blaming the agent.
features.say: Before we blame the AI, this shows who was on the call, where they connected from, and how the connection held up.
features.ask: When callers say the line broke up, how do you tell whether it was their signal or your system?
features.limits: Network-level view; conversational detail lives in Agent insights.
features.ask_technical: Do you need per-participant region and connection data exported into your own monitoring?

features.name: Agent Insights Timeline and Playback
features.does: Puts call audio, transcript, traces and logs on one synchronized timeline you can play and scrub turn by turn.
features.value: Replaces hours of stitching recordings, LLM consoles and server logs with one view.
features.say: This is the whole call on one timeline: you can hear it, read it, and see what the agent was doing at the exact same second.
features.ask: When someone reviews a bad call today, how many tools do they open to piece it together?
features.limits: Requires Agent observability enabled and LiveKit Agents SDK 1.3+; data kept 30 days.
features.ask_technical: Are your agents on Agents SDK 1.3+ and deployed to LiveKit Cloud or self-hosted workers?

features.name: Latency Breakdown and Distribution
features.does: Splits every reply into hearing (STT), knowing the caller finished (EOT), thinking (LLM TTFT) and speaking (TTS TTFB), and plots every turn so outliers stand out.
features.value: Tells you exactly which part to fix when the agent pauses awkwardly.
features.say: Every pause is broken down: how long to hear, to decide you'd finished, to think, and to start speaking. Here the average reply is about 1.5 seconds and you can see the one slow turn.
features.ask: When your agent pauses before answering, how do you figure out which part caused it?
features.limits: Backchannels show 'Not measured' unless adaptive interruption is enabled.
features.ask_technical: What reply latency target do you hold yourselves to, and at which percentile?

features.name: Transcript with Tool Calls
features.does: Turn-by-turn transcript with confidence, per-turn latency, agent handoffs and every tool call with its arguments and result.
features.value: See what the agent heard, what it looked up in your systems, and what came back.
features.say: Here's the conversation with how sure we were of every word the caller said, and here the agent looked up the customer's tickets: you see exactly what it asked your system and what it got back.
features.ask: When the agent looks something up in your systems and gets it wrong, how do you know whether it was the agent or the data?
use_cases: Catching mishearings of names and numbers
features.limits: Tool payloads are stored unless PII redaction is enabled.
features.ask_technical: Which backend calls would your agent make: REST tools, MCP servers, or both?

features.name: Traces and Prompt Context
features.does: Gantt chart of every pipeline stage per turn; each span shows duration, TTFT, model, and the exact chat context/instructions the LLM saw.
features.value: Fix bad answers with certainty because you see the prompt behind them.
features.say: Click the thinking step and you see the exact instructions and context the model had when it answered, plus how long it took.
features.ask: When the agent says something off-brand, how do you check what instructions it was actually following?
features.limits: Built on OpenTelemetry; disabled if OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true in the agent environment.
features.ask_technical: Do you also want these spans in your own APM (Datadog, Langfuse) via OpenTelemetry export?

features.name: Session Logs and Log Drains
features.does: Agent worker logs for the session aligned to the call timeline, with level filters; log drains capture crash and cross-replica logs.
features.value: Connect an error message to the exact moment the caller heard silence.
features.say: Your agent's own logs line up with the audio, so a warning sits right next to the moment the caller experienced it.
features.ask: When a call fails, how hard is it to connect the error log to what the caller actually heard?
features.limits: Session-scoped; set up a log drain for crash and cross-replica logs.
features.ask_technical: Where do your logs live today, and do you want a drain into that system?

features.name: Turn into a Test
features.does: Derives a simulation scenario (simulated caller + pass criteria) from this real call and downloads it as scenario.yaml.
features.value: Every bad call becomes a regression test so it can't happen again unnoticed.
features.say: Found a bad call? One click turns it into a repeatable test you run before every release.
features.ask: What's one call that went badly that you'd never want repeated?
use_cases: Building a test suite from production
features.limits: Takes ~10-20 s to generate; cancel in demos (don't download).
features.ask_technical: Would you check these scenarios into the repo and run them in CI with 'lk agent simulate'?

features.name: Share with LiveKit Support and Download Data
labels: Allow LiveKit support to access this page
features.does: Share a session with project admins or grant revocable LiveKit support access; export the session's audio, transcript and telemetry.
features.value: Fast support without sharing credentials; keep records beyond 30 days for compliance.
features.say: If you need our help, one checkbox lets our team see just this call, and you can revoke it anytime. And you can download everything for your own archive.
features.ask: Do you have to keep call recordings and transcripts in your own systems for compliance?
features.limits: Insights expire after 30 days unless downloaded or exported.
features.ask_technical: Would you rather stream recordings and transcripts to your own bucket continuously?

features.name: Fleet Health and Tails by Stage
features.does: Fleet-wide metrics and latency tails per stage; click a tail to open the matching sessions ranked worst first.
features.value: Go from 'some calls feel slow' to the exact worst calls in two clicks.
features.say: Across every call, this shows your slowest replies and which stage caused them, and one click lists the worst calls so you can listen to them.
features.ask: Which part of the call experience generates the most complaints about delays?
features.limits: Most charts need agent observability on; otherwise only session counts, connection latency, uptime and load show.
features.ask_technical: Do you track p95/p99 end-to-end latency today, and per which stage?

features.name: Compare Agents
features.does: Select agents or versions and compare latency composition and interruption rates side by side.
features.value: Pick the better prompt, model or voice with numbers, not opinions.
features.say: Trying a new prompt or voice? Put the two side by side and see which one is actually faster and interrupted less.
features.ask: When you try a new script or provider, how do you prove it's better before rolling it out?
features.limits: Needs two agents with sessions in the selected range; button stays disabled until two are selected.
features.ask_technical: Would you compare agents, or versions of the same agent via non-production deployments?

features.name: Observability Settings and Data Region
features.does: Project-wide switch for capturing traces, transcripts and audio, plus the data region where it is stored.
features.value: One decision for the whole project, with data kept in your chosen region.
features.say: One switch turns on full call recording and insight for the project, and you choose which region the data lives in.
features.ask: Who on your team decides what gets recorded, and are there regions your data must stay in?
features.limits: Applies to new sessions only; agents can opt out per session in code.
features.ask_technical: Do you need recording off for some agents or callers (per-session record options)?

features.name: PII Redaction (41 categories)
features.does: LLM-based redaction of 41 categories of personal data (names, contact, demographics, credentials, network, organization, financial, location, date, identifiers) from transcripts, traces and audio before storage.
features.value: Debug real calls without storing card numbers, SSNs or patient names; included at no extra cost.
features.say: Turn this on and sensitive details like card numbers, IDs and names are scrubbed from transcripts, traces and audio before anything is stored, across 41 categories, at no extra cost.
features.ask: What rules do you have about card numbers, patient names or IDs showing up in call transcripts?
features.limits: Off by default; new sessions only. Room names (e.g. caller numbers from individual dispatch rules) are not redacted.
features.ask_technical: Which categories must be redacted for you, and do you also need redaction in your own exported logs?

demo_instructions: 1. Frame it: when a customer says 'the agent was weird on my call', you need that exact call, not guesswork. Ask: 'Today, how long does it take you to find out what went wrong on one bad call?' 2. Go to Sessions from the main left sidebar (if you're inside an agent or builder page, click the project name in the breadcrumb first). Explain: every room/call in the project, searchable, with a time range (widen it to Past 7 days if the list is empty). 3. Open a call that has agent data: in the sessions list prefer a row whose Features column shows 'View agent insights' (widen the time range to Past 7 days if none do; skip console test rooms). Click its session ID. It lands on Session analytics: explain the top facts (room name, duration, unique participants, total participant minutes), the session timeline (who joined and left when), the participants (publishers and subscribers: the caller and the agent), egresses (recordings/streams) and the network panels: bandwidth and connection quality/latency. Value: rule out the network before blaming the AI. 4. Click Session events: the raw event log of the room (joins, tracks published, disconnects and their reasons). Value: exact answers like 'the caller dropped' vs 'the agent left'. 5. Click Agent insights: the agent's own view of the same call, on one timeline: the latency metrics and per-turn breakdown (speech-to-text, LLM, text-to-speech), then Transcript (every turn and tool call), Traces (each stage of a slow turn with the exact prompt), Logs, and audio playback. Point at the slowest turn. 6. Mention Share (send a call to a teammate or LiveKit support) and Turn into a test (make this call a Simulation so it never regresses). 7. Close: ask which recent call they'd want to look at first, and offer to set up observability on their project.
